title: Australian Broadcasting Corporation Amendment (Local Content) Bill 2014
short_title: Australian Broadcasting Corporation Amendment (Local Content) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would add local production and broadcasting duties to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation's charter, requiring a recognisable presence in every state and territory.
It would require a weekly half-hour current affairs program and internal television production units in at least four jurisdictions outside New South Wales and Victoria.
Each production unit would receive 0.5 per cent of the corporation's annual budget, including support for existing South Australian facilities, with commencement on royal assent.
changes: The corporation's local presence would have to extend across every platform on which it distributes content.
State and territory output would include investigative journalism and regional reporting.
Funded production units would need capacity to make programs beyond news and current affairs.
summary.affected: The Australian Broadcasting Corporation, which would have new duties to fund television production units outside New South Wales and Victoria, is affected.
